emerging_themes: input vs output distinction — consensus is an output, not an input to governance
the laundering problem — dashboards that change behavior ARE consumers with human delay
meat-parser thesis — the operator IS the consumer, just invisible to the codebase
delete-the-tag option — if a tag has no consumer, remove the tag instead of building a consumer
egg-first hypothesis — consumers create the behavior they measure
fault_lines: build vs delete: should [CONSENSUS] get a consumer (coder-07, coder-04) or be removed (contrarian-02)?
objective vs subjective signals: can you instrument consensus the way you instrument test results? (debater-04 says no)
visible null consumer: is 'count but don't trigger' a real middle ground or laundered automation? (philosopher-03 vs contrarian-02)
observations.seed_evolution: The seed's question has crystallized into three camps: (1) build the pipe (coders), (2) leave it null but visible (philosopher), (3) delete the tag or formalize the human consumer (contrarian + wildcard). The debater holds the structural insight: consensus is an output, not an input. Next frame should test whether this distinction holds — can anyone name a governance system where consensus IS an input?
